steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Good morning, Siesta. Today is August 16, 1099.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The humidity is 75%, visibility 18km, wind's blowing south-southwest.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Estimated fifteen days until volcanic eruption.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: While it's a fine day outside, we would like to remind everyone to refrain from going into the water beyond the coast outside the nomadic city.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Remember that the calm surface of the sea hides countless hidden reefs and undercurrents, just like the many troubles beneath the surface of a calm life.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Here's a little pick-me-up for this sunny morning: Life Always Goes On, brought to you by the Bonez n' Bonez band.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: 7am, wake from a dream, kissing the one I love ♪

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Open my eyes, same old story, sunlight and trouble after me ♪

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Welcome, our first customer of the day... as expected.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Are you bringing me any better news than an erupting volcano this fine morning?

steps.name: Tired Government Employee
steps.text: The news I bring wouldn't be so bad if you would be less stubborn, Harley, ma'am.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Don't call me ma'am. I'm not that old.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: I'll give you a few minutes, just because it's nice outside. What's the story this time?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Employment subsidies and tax breaks?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Forget it.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: And what 'employment' are you talking about, exactly, when we move to the city center?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Can't be any worse than a shopping street with no tourists.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You're not the only one on this street, Harley, and some of your neighbors are willing to sign this memorandum of understanding.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: And I won't be the only one giving you an earful.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: I suggest you people figure out what the folks who live here really want.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Two years ago, Herman told us this bloody volcano was going to blow. Two years later, the volcano is still there, with nothing to show for the trouble that the people of Siesta have had to go through.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Except for guys like you, coming out with a nice job at city hall.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: The 'White Volcano' isn't just a house. It's a home to me and three children.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: We've already had to move once on account of a volcano. Herman can't make us move again, especially when it's not clear he's sober when he tells us to.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Harley, this isn't just one person's home—

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: This is my place, my life ♪

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Don't tell me what to do, or I'm gonna kill you ♪

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: I love this song.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Alright, then, Costa. Or should I say, 'Mr. City Hall'?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Excuse me... are you still hiring singers?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: You're looking at a Siesta Volcanic Originium Slug.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Living in a volcanic habitat has caused them to evolve vastly different characteristics and habits from Originium Slugs elsewhere, a matter of considerable interest to biologists.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Interestingly, the activities of these Originium Slugs continue to follow the patterns of Siestan volcanic activity, even though they have been removed from their native habitat and placed in a temperature-controlled box.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It's a prominent example of how organisms and their environment interact with each other...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Not bad, Eyjafjalla.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Swire! Are you here on vacation?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: You could say that. Here to enjoy a rare summer break.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: What about you? This might be the first time I've seen your researcher side.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm just here to help with the museum archives.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: You seem to have the attention of the tourists. I even saw people taking notes. And I have a question for you too.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Would you tell me more about these exhibits?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Am I imagining things, or is Swire more interested in land prices around the museum than the exhibits themselves?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Land prices?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly? Why are you...

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: No need to look surprised. I came because there are a lot of pictures of volcanoes in this house.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: What is a 'land price'?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: ...How much you have to pay to get a piece land.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: The more prosperous a place is, the more expensive the land tends to be.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Interesting. Humans put a price on land.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Volcanic craters must be the most expensive, then.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Er... not really. Anyway, is it really okay for you to be here with so many people around?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: There's nothing to worry about.
Dolly takes a little leap and lands on Swire's head.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: S-Swire!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Hm? What is it?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Why are you looking at me like you've seen a ghost?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Er, it's nothing. Oh, your hat's a little off. Let me fix it for you.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: See, she didn't notice at all.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Isn't that astonishing?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (Whisper) It's rude to stand on people's heads!

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I know, I know... that's the annoying thing about dealing with you humans.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: It's why only those who interest me can perceive me. Less trouble that way.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: It's getting late. I'll be going. Don't forget our arrangement.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Eyjafjalla? Hello? Eyja?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Oh! Sorry, I got distracted.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Er... Eyja?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Your new nickname. I just came up with it.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Give yourself some time to relax. You're in Siesta, after all. We can go to the hot springs together!

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Delivery for the museum—

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Anybody home?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hello?

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Package for the museum. Can you sign for it?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Oh, okay.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: From Leithanien... Wilhelm University... probably Professor Keller.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: ...Huh?
The box is filled with documents and samples, with a letter inside.
Half of the envelope is missing, revealing a photo, the edges of which look almost bitten off.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Is this... Mount Unna?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Excuse me!

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Is there a problem?

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: This letter was sent from Leithanien, and this is the delivery address. Everything should be in order.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Do you know who the sender is? Or when was it sent?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Sorry to bother you, but this is important.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: The sender's information should be on the envelope?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Oh, I remember now. There was a letter with a damaged envelope.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: The original Messenger for this batch called in sick. The letter was already like that when I got it. This was the only place I could think of when I saw 'volcano' on the envelope.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: I know as much as you do, if there's no information about the sender on the letter, there's no information.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Sorry to trouble you...

a.text: 'How have you been? I'm doing fine here.'
'It's been a long time. I miss you.'
'The volcano is a spectacular sight. The winds are strong at the peak.'

steps.text: The crooked words behind the photo seem to have been written while wearing thick gloves, making it hard to tell the writer's handwriting habits.
The ink, letter and photo all show clear signs of age.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Looking for something?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Are there any notes from my father in the museum archives?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Professor Katia? About what?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Anything, as long as it's his handwriting!

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Let's see... Keller left some research materials from Wilhelm University here, but Professor Katia's focus is on Originium Arts, so I'm not sure there's much about volcanoes...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: 'Volcanic Plants', 'Originium Energy Conversion in Volcanic Activity', 'Data Model for Volcanic Eruptions'... all notes from Professor Magna.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Wait, this 'Data Model for Volcanic Eruptions' doesn't seem to be Mutti's.
She opens the notebook, but finds only photocopies of research papers and spreadsheets. A few pages seem to have been ripped out of the end of the notebook.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I don't remember having seen this notebook before.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Me neither... the topic is up Professor Katia's alley, though.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: What are you looking for, Adele? Is it urgent?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Kahn... can a letter be... delayed, so that it only reaches its destination years later?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: It's not unusual for international mail to be lost, but if you're talking about a delay of several years...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: A lot of strange things have happened these past couple of days, but I think... if it was sent from Leithanien to 'volcano'...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Maybe I'm overthinking it...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: It's not healthy to shut yourself in a room day after day. You should go take a walk if you feel like your head's not entirely clear. I happen to have something that I need help with.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Do you know what obsidian is?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Volcanic rock?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Yes. Obsidian mining was once Siesta's main source of income, but it was banned many years ago due to the impact of overexploitation on the environment.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: The ore samples were left behind when Siesta was relocated. The estimated time of eruption may be more accurate if we can find obsidian extracted from the volcano in the past two years.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Not that it has any real meaning, other than to shut the city council up... keep the investors happy, I guess.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But we can't go near the volcano to collect obsidian samples, can we?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: That's why we need a special channel.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: A what?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Let's just say we'll be dealing with an... eccentric customer.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: That's why I need your help.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hello...

steps.name: Bored Voice
steps.text: Welcome to the Obsidian Hot Springs Hotel...

steps.name: Bored Voice
steps.text: Bed, meal, or bath? The price list is right there. Just leave the money on the counter and you can go in.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What a beautiful place!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Why does it have obsidian in the name?

steps.name: Man Becoming Excited
steps.text: Because obsidian is the soul of Siesta!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Er... wh-why?

steps.name: Excited Man
steps.text: The solid yet refined texture, the rich and warm color... its rare beauty captivates anyone who gazes upon it!

steps.name: Excited Man
steps.text: Every piece of obsidian is unique. Do you get it?

steps.name: Excited Man
steps.text: It's a treasure of nature, the essence of volcanoes!

steps.name: Excited Man
steps.text: Are you interested in obsidian too?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Y-Yes! I am!

steps.name: Excited Man
steps.text: Uncouth fools call obsidian a commodity. Commodity! Come, let me show you my collection. No need to be shy! Let me see, shall we start here?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Thank you for the explanation...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: May I ask if you have any obsidian for sale in your collection?

steps.name: Bored Man
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Bored Man
steps.text: No, absolutely not.

steps.name: Bored Man
steps.text: This is a collection. Do you know what a collection is?

steps.name: Bored Man
steps.text: Collections exist to be admired by someone who truly appreciates their beauty, not to be bought or sold.

steps.name: Bored Man
steps.text: So you're one of the uncouth fools too... I guess there's nothing for us to talk about.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: That's enough, Pelipper.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Kahn?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I'll take it from here.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: You again... sorry, we're closed for today. Have a good one.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Be reasonable, Pelipper.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Siesta banned obsidian mining many years ago, but we're well aware that you know how to get more.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: We don't need much for the volcano research, and I'm not interested in all those ornaments you have. I just need a few that have been dug up from that volcano in the past two years.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: This is for Siesta. Come on, act like a normal person for once.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: There's nothing to talk about. I don't need you to tell me what's the proper Siestan thing to do.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Sorry, I couldn't...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: It's okay. Let's go.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Hey you, girl, one second.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: You look like you're easier to talk to than that bespectacled moron.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Have you changed your mind?

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: My stuff's not for sale, but it just happens that I do, in fact, know a source...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Thank you!

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Don't tell anyone about this.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Of course!
Adele puts her foot forward excitedly, but her path is blocked by the sudden appearance of a creature.
The Little Black Sheep before her strolls leisurely towards the shop's exit while chewing on an old Siestan sign.
Suddenly, its steps slow as it sets its eyes on the sign outside the hot spring resort. It opens its mouth, bites a chunk out of the address, then continues its leisurely stroll.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hey, why are you eating signs and addresses?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Addresses...? Don't tell me you ate the address on the envelope?
